name: Tennessee divorce: alimony, property and parenting
description: Tennessee family law: classification and division of marital property including retirement benefits (Cohen, Batson), types of alimony (Burlew, Crabtree, Gonsewski), and modification of parenting schedules on a material change in circumstances.

name: Public trial and press access to proceedings
description: Openness of criminal proceedings: the First Amendment right of access (Richmond Newspapers, Globe Newspaper, Press-Enterprise I and II), the Sixth Amendment public-trial right and closure findings (Waller, Washington's Bone-Club factors), and the common-law right to judicial records (Nixon v. Warner Communications).

name: Federal habeas: AEDPA deference and procedural default
description: Federal collateral review under AEDPA: unreasonable application of clearly established law (Williams v. Taylor, Harrington, Pinholster), procedural default and cause (Coleman, Murray v. Carrier), certificates of appealability (Slack, Miller-El), Brecht harmlessness, and Strickland/Wiggins and Brady/Kyles claims.

name: Eyewitness identification and lineups
description: Pretrial identification: the right to counsel at post-indictment lineups (Wade, Gilbert, Kirby), suggestive procedures and due process (Stovall, Simmons, Foster), and reliability under Neil v. Biggers and Manson v. Brathwaite.

name: Apprendi: jury findings and the statutory maximum
description: The immediate Apprendi wave: facts increasing a penalty beyond the statutory maximum must go to a jury, the prior-conviction exception (Almendarez-Torres), and plain-error and harmless-error treatment of Apprendi errors (Johnson, Neder, Cotton, Olano).

name: Equal protection: rational basis and classifications
description: Equal protection outside race: rational-basis review of economic and welfare classifications (Williamson v. Lee Optical, Dandridge, Lindsley, Fritz), right-to-travel durational residency (Shapiro, Dunn), education (Rodriguez, Plyler), age (Murgia), alienage (Graham) and Cleburne.

name: Washington torts: government duty and the CPA
description: Washington tort precedent on public entities' duties: take-charge duties of parole and probation officers (Taggart, Hertog), the public-duty doctrine (Taylor), and Consumer Protection Act claims (Hangman Ridge elements, Bain on deeds of trust).

name: California sentencing reform and resentencing (2020s)
description: California's 2018-2022 sentencing changes: retroactive ameliorative statutes under In re Estrada, discretion to strike enhancements (Romero, Carmony), ability to pay fines (Dueñas), and youth-offender issues after Miller (Gutierrez).

name: Feres doctrine and Bivens remedies
description: Limits on suing the United States and its officers: the Feres bar on service-related claims under the FTCA (Brooks, Brown, Stencel, Shearer) and its Bivens counterpart (Chappell, Stanley), prisoner FTCA claims (Muniz), Bivens and its alternatives (Carlson, Bush v. Lucas, Schweiker v. Chilicky).

name: Harmless error and structural error (1995)
description: Mid-1990s harmless-error doctrine: Chapman's beyond-reasonable-doubt test, Brecht and Kotteakos on collateral review, structural errors like a defective reasonable-doubt instruction (Sullivan v. Louisiana) and denial of counsel (Gideon, Faretta), and Fulminante.

name: Louisiana civil: insurance interpretation and malpractice
description: Louisiana civil precedent: insurance policies construed by plain meaning and ambiguities against the insurer (Reynolds v. Select Properties), summary judgment (Schroeder, Samaha) and medical malpractice causation.

name: Eleventh Circuit: adopting former Fifth Circuit precedent
description: Early Eleventh Circuit criminal appeals (1980s) whose common thread is Bonner v. City of Prichard: decisions of the former Fifth Circuit handed down before October 1, 1981 are binding precedent in the Eleventh Circuit; with extrinsic-act evidence (Beechum) and indictments (Hamling).

name: Habeas timeliness and equitable tolling
description: AEDPA's one-year limitations period: equitable tolling for extraordinary circumstances (Holland, Pace, Rose v. Lee), actual-innocence gateways (Schlup), second or successive petitions (Slack, Gonzalez v. Crosby) and certificates of appealability (Miller-El); Fourth Circuit heavy.

name: Louisiana prescription and asbestos claims
description: Louisiana prescription (statutes of limitation) and contra non valentem (Corsey, Carter, Campo), asbestos exposure and causation, insurance trigger (Cole v. Celotex), and limits on retroactive legislation.

name: Oregon statutory interpretation
description: Oregon's interpretive method: PGE's text-and-context first level, modified by State v. Gaines to allow legislative history, the court's duty to find the correct interpretation (Stull), and avoiding surplusage (Cloutier).

name: New York premises liability
description: New York negligence on summary judgment: actual and constructive notice of a dangerous condition (Gordon v. American Museum, Piacquadio), contractors' duties to third parties (Espinal), intervening causes (Derdiarian), and the Alvarez/Winegrad/Zuckerman burdens.

name: Texas parental-rights termination
description: Termination of parental rights in Texas: statutory endangerment grounds under § 161.001(1), the Holley best-interest factors, clear-and-convincing evidence and heightened sufficiency review (In re C.H., In re J.F.C.), and incarceration as endangerment (Boyd).

name: Texas default judgments and restricted appeals
description: Setting aside default judgments in Texas under Craddock v. Sunshine Bus Lines (no conscious indifference, meritorious defense, no undue delay), lack of notice (Peralta), defective service, bills of review and restricted appeals.

name: Florida divorce: equitable distribution and alimony
description: Florida domestic-relations law: equitable distribution and lump-sum alimony (Canakaris, including its abuse-of-discretion test), competent substantial evidence (Shaw v. Shaw), and attorney's fee lodestar findings (Florida Patient's Compensation Fund v. Rowe).

name: Double jeopardy: same offense and multiple punishment
description: The Double Jeopardy Clause: Blockburger's same-elements test, multiple punishments and legislative intent (Whalen, Albernaz, Missouri v. Hunter), successive prosecutions (Brown v. Ohio, Grady, Dixon), collateral estoppel (Ashe), incorporation (Benton) and vindictive resentencing (Pearce).

name: Qualified immunity and § 1983 officer liability
description: Suits against officials under § 1983 from Monroe v. Pape onward: qualified immunity and clearly established law (Harlow, Anderson v. Creighton, Pearson, Hope), interlocutory appeal of its denial (Forsyth, Johnson v. Jones), excessive and deadly force (Graham, Scott v. Harris) and municipal liability (Monell).

name: Right to appointed counsel (1970s)
description: The right to counsel after Gideon: misdemeanors with imprisonment (Argersinger, Scott v. Illinois), waiver (Zerbst, Carnley), self-representation (Faretta), uncounseled prior convictions (Burgett, Loper), and denial of consultation during an overnight recess (Geders).

name: Texas Anders briefs (1990s-2000s)
description: Anders and Penson as applied in Texas: what an Anders brief must contain (High, Currie, Stafford), the appellate court's independent review (Bledsoe), and notice-of-appeal limits on what can be raised.

name: Federal Indian law and tribal sovereignty
description: Tribal sovereignty and state authority in Indian country: Worcester v. Georgia, infringement of tribal self-government (Williams v. Lee), state taxation (McClanahan, Moe, Colville, Bracker), tribal jurisdiction over nonmembers (Montana, Oliphant), sovereign immunity and ICRA (Santa Clara Pueblo, Wheeler).

name: Ohio postconviction relief and res judicata
description: Ohio's bar on relitigating in postconviction proceedings claims that could have been raised on direct appeal (State v. Perry, Cole), postconviction petitions (Calhoun), and resentencing for post-release control (Bezak, Fischer).

name: Eleventh Circuit sentencing reasonableness
description: Eleventh Circuit review of federal sentences after Booker: substantive reasonableness (Talley, Pugh, Irey en banc), within-range sentences as indicators of reasonableness, and the Bonner v. City of Prichard rule adopting pre-October 1981 Fifth Circuit decisions as binding.

name: California capital appeals
description: California Supreme Court review of death judgments: Ring's jury-finding requirement for aggravating circumstances and the state court's repeated rejection of challenges to California's death-penalty statute, with Watson harmlessness.

name: Texas criminal: ineffective assistance on direct appeal
description: Strickland as applied by the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals: a silent record on direct appeal rarely shows deficient performance (Thompson, Bone, Goodspeed, Mallett), so counsel's conduct is presumed strategic unless it was so outrageous no competent attorney would engage in it.

name: Commerce Clause: limits on Congress (Lopez era)
description: The reach of Congress's commerce power after Lopez and Morrison: aggregation (Wickard, Perez, Heart of Atlanta), jurisdictional elements in federal crimes (Bass, Jones v. United States arson, Scarborough firearms nexus), and the Tenth Amendment.

name: Sufficiency review in Georgia and Louisiana criminal appeals
description: Jackson v. Virginia sufficiency as applied by Georgia and Louisiana courts: the jury resolves conflicts and judges credibility, and the appellate court asks only whether any rational trier of fact could find the elements proved.

name: Antitrust: Sherman Act restraints and antitrust injury
description: Sherman and Clayton Act doctrine: per se rules versus the rule of reason (Socony-Vacuum, Board of Trade, Topco, Professional Engineers), vertical restraints (Schwinn, Continental T.V., Monsanto), tying (Northern Pacific, Jefferson Parish v. Hyde), intra-enterprise conspiracy (Copperweld) and antitrust injury (Brunswick, AGC v. Carpenters).

name: Article III standing
description: Standing doctrine: injury in fact, traceability and redressability (Lujan, Warth, Allen, Simon), taxpayer and organizational standing (Valley Forge, Havens), future injury and injunctions (Lyons, Clapper's 'certainly impending'), environmental plaintiffs (Friends of the Earth, Steel Co.) and concreteness (Spokeo).

name: New York criminal appeals: weight, preservation, counsel
description: Sub-cluster form of the New York Court of Appeals criminal line: weight-of-the-evidence review (Bleakley, Danielson), the specific-objection preservation rule for sufficiency (Gray, Hawkins) and meaningful representation (Baldi, Benevento).

name: Labor arbitration: Steelworkers Trilogy
description: Arbitration under collective-bargaining agreements: the Steelworkers Trilogy, § 301 enforcement (Lincoln Mills), procedural arbitrability for arbitrators (Wiley v. Livingston), no-strike injunctions (Boys Markets) and deference to awards (Misco, W.R. Grace).

name: Plain error and new rules on direct review (1995)
description: Rule 52(b) after Olano: plain error judged at the time of appeal when the law changes (Johnson v. United States after Gaudin's materiality-to-the-jury rule), new rules on direct review (Griffith), and inconsistent verdicts.

name: Dormant Commerce Clause
description: State laws burdening interstate commerce: discrimination and economic protectionism (Philadelphia v. New Jersey, Hughes, Oregon Waste, Carbone v. Clarkstown), the Pike balancing test, state taxes (Complete Auto v. Brady, Bacchus, Limbach) and the market-participant line (Exxon v. Maryland).

name: Mississippi divorce: equitable distribution and custody
description: Mississippi domestic-relations law: equitable distribution under the Ferguson factors and classification of marital assets (Hemsley), alimony after division (Armstrong, Johnson v. Johnson), grounds for divorce, and the Albright custody factors.

name: New York no-fault serious injury
description: Summary judgment on 'serious injury' under New York Insurance Law § 5102(d): objective proof of significant limitation (Toure, Licari, Gaddy), gaps in treatment and preexisting conditions (Pommells, Perl), and admissible medical reports (Grasso).

name: California civil appeals and the Bane Act
description: California appellate presumptions (Denham's presumption of correctness, Jameson on the record), relief from default (Rappleyea), and Bane Act civil-rights claims requiring coercion and specific intent.

name: Patent obviousness and PTAB review
description: Obviousness under § 103 after KSR (Graham factors, motivation to combine, hindsight), Federal Circuit substantial-evidence review of PTAB and examiner fact-finding (Gartside, Nuvasive, Intelligent Bio-Systems), and inter partes review (SAS Institute v. Iancu).

name: Arizona criminal appeals: fundamental error and capital review
description: Arizona Supreme Court criminal precedent: fundamental-error review of unobjected-to error (Henderson), Anders/Leon full-record review, and capital-case issues (Gretzler, Bible's Frye ruling, Atwood).

name: Mandamus, supplemental jurisdiction and federal-court power
description: Supervisory mandamus over district courts (Roche, La Buy, Schlagenhauf, Will, Kerr), review of remand orders (Thermtron v. Hermansdorfer), the amount in controversy (St. Paul Mercury, Zahn), and supplemental jurisdiction after dismissing federal claims (Gibbs, Cohill).

name: Asylum: persecution and nexus (Ninth Circuit)
description: Circuit review of asylum denials, mainly in the Ninth Circuit: persecution on account of a protected ground and nexus (Elias-Zacarias), well-founded fear (Cardoza-Fonseca, Stevic), corroboration after the REAL ID Act, and remand to the agency (INS v. Ventura).

name: New Jersey criminal sentencing and trial error
description: New Jersey criminal precedent: sentencing review of aggravating and mitigating factors (State v. Roth, Fuentes, Case), consecutive sentences (Yarbough), prosecutorial summation (Frost), and cumulative error (Weaver).

name: Copyright: originality, infringement and fair use
description: Copyright law: originality (Feist), idea versus expression (Baker v. Selden, Computer Associates v. Altai), fair use (Sony, Harper & Row, Campbell v. Acuff-Rose), derivative works (Stewart v. Abend), fee awards (Fogerty), and online secondary liability (Perfect 10).

name: Massachusetts civil: summary judgment and implied covenant
description: Massachusetts summary-judgment burdens (Kourouvacilis, Pederson), the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing (Anthony's Pier Four), and premises and negligence duties (Mullins).

name: Virginia Court of Appeals criminal review
description: Virginia criminal appeals: deciding on the best and narrowest grounds, sufficiency and the reasonable-hypothesis-of-innocence rule for circumstantial evidence (Haskins, Higginbotham), viewing the whole record (Bolden), and hearsay exceptions (Martin).

name: California civil: employment, premises duty and summary judgment
description: California civil precedent: summary judgment (Aguilar), FEHA discrimination and retaliation (Guz, Yanowitz, Harris v. Santa Monica), and the duty and foreseeability analysis for premises liability (Rowland, Ann M., Saelzler).

name: Civil forfeiture, double jeopardy and excessive fines
description: Whether civil sanctions are punishment: civil penalties and forfeitures under the Double Jeopardy Clause (Halper, Kurth Ranch, Ursery, Hudson), forfeiture under the Excessive Fines Clause (Austin), and innocent-owner forfeiture (Calero-Toledo).
